column11: measured from CMS Part D, which the book already carries for rimegepant (partd_prescribing, asset 202, cms_brands 'Nurtec Odt' / 'Rimegepant Sulfate', data year 2024): national total drug cost 625,015,501.30 USD across 105,287 national beneficiaries. 625,015,501.30 / 105,287 = 5,936.30 USD a beneficiary a year. The series is stable and rising with price: 4,892.88 USD in 2022 and 5,706.75 in 2023 on the same two fields. CMS states total drug cost is gross of manufacturer rebates, so this is a list-equivalent figure and the gross_to_net_pct row below still applies on top of it. Cross-check against the unit price rather than derivation from it: Pfizer's own disclosure is 1,028.99 USD per blister pack of eight 75 mg orally disintegrating tablets (Connecticut HB 6669, data as of 13-Jan-2025), that is 128.62 USD a dose, so 5,936.30 USD is about 46 doses a year, against the label ceiling of 18 doses in any 30 days
column12: the Part D population is Medicare, so it skews to 65 and over and to the disabled under 65, while migraine is mostly a working-age disease.
